prompt: Analyze frequently purchased product combinations to identify common bundles in the sales data. Compare co-purchase patterns across store locations and seasonal periods to reveal location- and season-specific buying behavior.
title: Co-Purchase Bundle Analysis
summary: Analyze frequently purchased product combinations to identify common bundles in the sales data. Compare co-purchase patterns across store locations and seasonal periods to reveal location- and season-specific buying behavior.
executed_sql_queries:
WITH filtered_orders AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT o.order_id
    FROM retail.orders o
    WHERE o.order_date BETWEEN DATE '2020-01-01' AND DATE '2026-12-31'
),
order_pairs AS (
    SELECT
        oi1.order_id,
        oi1.product_id AS product_id_1,
        oi2.product_id AS product_id_2
    FROM retail.order_items oi1
    JOIN retail.order_items oi2
      ON oi1.order_id = oi2.order_id
     AND oi1.product_id < oi2.product_id
    JOIN filtered_orders fo
      ON fo.order_id = oi1.order_id
),
pair_counts AS (
    SELECT
        product_id_1,
        product_id_2,
        COUNT(DISTINCT order_id) AS co_purchase_frequency
    FROM order_pairs
    GROUP BY product_id_1, product_id_2
),
total_orders AS (
    SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT order_id) AS total_order_count
    FROM retail.orders
    WHERE order_date BETWEEN DATE '2020-01-01' AND DATE '2026-12-31'
)
SELECT
    p1.product_name AS product_name_1,
    p2.product_name AS product_name_2,
    pc.co_purchase_frequency,
    ROUND(pc.co_purchase_frequency::numeric / NULLIF(to2.total_order_count, 0), 6) AS order_share,
    RANK() OVER (ORDER BY pc.co_purchase_frequency DESC, p1.product_name, p2.product_name) AS bundle_rank
FROM pair_counts pc
JOIN retail.products p1 ON p1.product_id = pc.product_id_1
JOIN retail.products p2 ON p2.product_id = pc.product_id_2
CROSS JOIN total_orders to2
ORDER BY bundle_rank
LIMIT 20;
SELECT store_id, store_name, is_online FROM retail.stores ORDER BY store_id;

WITH store_orders AS (
    SELECT o.order_id, o.store_id, s.store_name
    FROM retail.orders o
    JOIN retail.stores s ON s.store_id = o.store_id
    WHERE s.store_name IN (
        'Zava Retail Seattle',
        'Zava Retail Bellevue',
        'Zava Retail Tacoma',
        'Zava Retail Spokane',
        'Zava Retail Everett',
        'Zava Retail Redmond',
        'Zava Retail Kirkland',
        'Zava Retail Online'
    )
), store_order_counts AS (
    SELECT store_id, COUNT(*) AS total_orders
    FROM store_orders
    GROUP BY store_id
), pair_counts AS (
    SELECT
        so.store_id,
        so.store_name,
        oi1.product_id AS product_id_1,
        oi2.product_id AS product_id_2,
        COUNT(DISTINCT so.order_id) AS store_level_co_purchase_frequency
    FROM store_orders so
    JOIN retail.order_items oi1 ON oi1.order_id = so.order_id
    JOIN retail.order_items oi2 ON oi2.order_id = so.order_id AND oi1.product_id < oi2.product_id
    GROUP BY so.store_id, so.store_name, oi1.product_id, oi2.product_id
), ranked AS (
    SELECT
        pc.*,
        ROUND(pc.store_level_co_purchase_frequency::numeric / soc.total_orders, 6) AS store_level_order_share,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY pc.store_name ORDER BY pc.store_level_co_purchase_frequency DESC, pc.product_id_1, pc.product_id_2) AS rn
    FROM pair_counts pc
    JOIN store_order_counts soc ON soc.store_id = pc.store_id
)
SELECT
    r.store_name,
    p1.product_name AS product_name_1,
    p2.product_name AS product_name_2,
    r.store_level_co_purchase_frequency,
    r.store_level_order_share
FROM ranked r
JOIN retail.products p1 ON p1.product_id = r.product_id_1
JOIN retail.products p2 ON p2.product_id = r.product_id_2
WHERE r.rn <= 10
ORDER BY r.store_name, r.store_level_co_purchase_frequency DESC, product_name_1, product_name_2;

WITH order_season AS (
    SELECT
        o.order_id,
        CASE
            WHEN EXTRACT(MONTH FROM o.order_date) IN (12, 1, 2) THEN 'Winter'
            WHEN EXTRACT(MONTH FROM o.order_date) IN (3, 4, 5) THEN 'Spring'
            WHEN EXTRACT(MONTH FROM o.order_date) IN (6, 7, 8) THEN 'Summer'
            ELSE 'Fall'
        END AS season
    FROM retail.orders o
    WHERE o.order_date BETWEEN DATE '2020-01-01' AND DATE '2026-12-31'
)
SELECT season, COUNT(DISTINCT order_id) AS total_orders
FROM order_season
GROUP BY season
ORDER BY season;

WITH order_season AS (
    SELECT
        o.order_id,
        CASE
            WHEN EXTRACT(MONTH FROM o.order_date) IN (12, 1, 2) THEN 'Winter'
            WHEN EXTRACT(MONTH FROM o.order_date) IN (3, 4, 5) THEN 'Spring'
            WHEN EXTRACT(MONTH FROM o.order_date) IN (6, 7, 8) THEN 'Summer'
            ELSE 'Fall'
        END AS season
    FROM retail.orders o
    WHERE o.order_date BETWEEN DATE '2020-01-01' AND DATE '2026-12-31'
),
season_totals AS (
    SELECT season, COUNT(DISTINCT order_id) AS total_orders
    FROM order_season
    GROUP BY season
),
pairs AS (
    SELECT
        os.season,
        oi1.product_id AS product_id_1,
        oi2.product_id AS product_id_2,
        COUNT(DISTINCT oi1.order_id) AS co_purchase_frequency
    FROM order_season os
    JOIN retail.order_items oi1
      ON oi1.order_id = os.order_id
    JOIN retail.order_items oi2
      ON oi2.order_id = os.order_id
     AND oi1.product_id < oi2.product_id
    GROUP BY os.season, oi1.product_id, oi2.product_id
),
ranked AS (
    SELECT
        p.season,
        p.product_id_1,
        pr1.product_name AS product_name_1,
        p.product_id_2,
        pr2.product_name AS product_name_2,
        p.co_purchase_frequency,
        ROUND(p.co_purchase_frequency::numeric / st.total_orders, 6) AS season_level_order_share,
        DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY p.season ORDER BY p.co_purchase_frequency DESC, p.product_id_1, p.product_id_2) AS bundle_rank
    FROM pairs p
    JOIN season_totals st ON st.season = p.season
    JOIN retail.products pr1 ON pr1.product_id = p.product_id_1
    JOIN retail.products pr2 ON pr2.product_id = p.product_id_2
)
SELECT *
FROM ranked
WHERE bundle_rank <= 10
ORDER BY season, bundle_rank, product_id_1, product_id_2;

WITH order_base AS (
  SELECT
    o.order_id,
    s.store_name,
    CASE
      WHEN EXTRACT(MONTH FROM o.order_date) IN (12,1,2) THEN 'Winter'
      WHEN EXTRACT(MONTH FROM o.order_date) IN (3,4,5) THEN 'Spring'
      WHEN EXTRACT(MONTH FROM o.order_date) IN (6,7,8) THEN 'Summer'
      ELSE 'Fall'
    END AS season
  FROM retail.orders o
  JOIN retail.stores s ON s.store_id = o.store_id
  WHERE o.order_date BETWEEN DATE '2020-01-01' AND DATE '2026-12-31'
), pair_orders AS (
  SELECT
    ob.store_name,
    ob.season,
    oi1.order_id,
    p1.product_name AS product_name_1,
    p2.product_name AS product_name_2
  FROM order_base ob
  JOIN retail.order_items oi1 ON oi1.order_id = ob.order_id
  JOIN retail.order_items oi2 ON oi2.order_id = ob.order_id AND oi1.product_id < oi2.product_id
  JOIN retail.products p1 ON p1.product_id = oi1.product_id
  JOIN retail.products p2 ON p2.product_id = oi2.product_id
), pair_counts AS (
  SELECT
    store_name,
    season,
    product_name_1,
    product_name_2,
    COUNT(DISTINCT order_id) AS store_season_co_purchase_frequency
  FROM pair_orders
  GROUP BY store_name, season, product_name_1, product_name_2
), store_season_totals AS (
  SELECT
    store_name,
    season,
    COUNT(DISTINCT order_id) AS total_orders
  FROM order_base
  GROUP BY store_name, season
), ranked AS (
  SELECT
    pc.store_name,
    pc.season,
    pc.product_name_1,
    pc.product_name_2,
    pc.store_season_co_purchase_frequency,
    ROUND(pc.store_season_co_purchase_frequency::numeric / NULLIF(sst.total_orders, 0), 6) AS store_season_order_share,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
      PARTITION BY pc.store_name, pc.season
      ORDER BY pc.store_season_co_purchase_frequency DESC, pc.product_name_1, pc.product_name_2
    ) AS rn
  FROM pair_counts pc
  JOIN store_season_totals sst
    ON sst.store_name = pc.store_name AND sst.season = pc.season
)
SELECT
  store_name,
  season,
  product_name_1,
  product_name_2,
  store_season_co_purchase_frequency,
  store_season_order_share
FROM ranked
WHERE rn <= 10
ORDER BY store_name, season, store_season_co_purchase_frequency DESC, product_name_1, product_name_2;

components.content:
Executive summary: The strongest co-purchased bundle overall is Wood Rasp Set + Digital Caliper 6-inch, appearing 7 times with an order share of 0.001347. The next-best bundles are tied at 6 co-purchases: Ball Peen Hammer 12oz + Pipe Wrench Set and Precision Screwdriver Kit + Metric Hex Key Set (each 0.001155 order share).

Top bundle patterns:

  • Precision/measuring tools recur frequently: Digital Caliper 6-inch + Metric Hex Key Set, Precision Screwdriver Kit + T-Handle Hex Set, and Tape Measure 25-foot + Speed Square 7-inch.
  • Hand tool pairings are also strong, especially Ball Peen Hammer 12oz + Pipe Wrench Set and Flathead Screwdriver Set + Riffler File Set.
  • Home improvement bundles show up consistently, such as Bathroom Lavatory Faucet + PTFE Thread Tape White, Moisture Resistant Drywall + Fire Resistant Drywall, and Oil-Based Wood Stain + Paint Bucket Grid.

Seasonal highlights: Spring and Summer show the clearest peak bundles. In Spring, Tape Measure 25-foot + Speed Square 7-inch leads with 4 co-purchases and the highest seasonal share at 0.003096. In Summer, two bundles tie for first at 4 co-purchases: Ball Peen Hammer 12oz + Pipe Wrench Set and Wood Rasp Set + Digital Caliper 6-inch, each at 0.003113.

Store-level concentration: At Zava Retail Redmond, the same core bundles dominate, led by Wood Rasp Set + Digital Caliper 6-inch (7) and the two 6-frequency bundles above. This suggests the strongest bundles are not isolated anomalies but repeatable cross-sell opportunities at the store level.

Bottom line: The data points to a clear bundle strategy around precision tools, measuring/layout tools, and complementary trade hardware. The most actionable cross-sells are the top 3 bundles, especially those with 6–7 co-purchases and order shares above 0.0011.

components.content:
Key merchandising takeaways: the strongest recurring co-purchase patterns are concentrated in a few tool-and-measurement bundles and a handful of seasonal project bundles. Across the full dataset, the top bundle is Wood Rasp Set + Digital Caliper 6-inch with 7 co-purchases and an order share of 0.1347%. Two bundles tie next at 6 co-purchases each: Ball Peen Hammer 12oz + Pipe Wrench Set and Precision Screwdriver Kit + Metric Hex Key Set (each 0.1155% order share).

Store-level insight: Zava Retail Redmond mirrors the overall pattern almost exactly, indicating these bundles are not isolated anomalies. Redmond’s top bundle is also Wood Rasp Set + Digital Caliper 6-inch at 7, followed by the same two 6-order bundles. This suggests a strong opportunity for store-specific endcaps, cross-sell prompts, and “frequently bought together” online placement in Redmond for precision tools, wrenching, and screwdriver/hex assortments.

Seasonal opportunities:

  • Spring: the highest seasonal bundle is Tape Measure 25-foot + Speed Square 7-inch with 4 co-purchases and the highest seasonal order share at 0.3096%. This is a clear candidate for framing/carpentry promo packs.
  • Summer: two bundles lead at 4 co-purchases each: Ball Peen Hammer 12oz + Pipe Wrench Set and Wood Rasp Set + Digital Caliper 6-inch, both at 0.3113%. Summer messaging should emphasize repair, plumbing, and precision-measurement kits.
  • Fall: the top bundle is Precision Screwdriver Kit + Tape Measure 25-foot at 3 co-purchases and 0.2346%. Fall also shows strong home-improvement and garden pairings such as Angled Brush Set + Metal Paint Tray 9-inch and Ceramic Planter 12-inch + Organic Heirloom Seeds.
  • Winter: the leading bundle is Wall Mount Cabinet + Magnetic Tool Holder with 4 co-purchases and 0.2983%. Winter is the best season for storage/organization bundles and electrical/plumbing maintenance add-ons.

Actionable recommendations:

  • Bundle precision tools together year-round: promote Digital Caliper 6-inch, Metric Hex Key Set, T-Handle Hex Set, and Precision Screwdriver Kit as a family. These appear repeatedly in both overall and Redmond results.
  • Build seasonal kits: Spring carpentry kit (Tape Measure + Speed Square), Summer repair kit (Pipe Wrench + Ball Peen Hammer), Fall finishing kit (Brush Set + Paint Tray), Winter organization kit (Wall Mount Cabinet + Magnetic Tool Holder).
  • Use store-specific signage in Redmond: prioritize the top 10 recurring bundles in aisle signage and POS recommendations, since Redmond matches the top overall bundles and shows repeated co-purchase frequencies of 3 to 7.
  • Cross-merchandise by project type: pair plumbing items (PTFE Thread Tape, Pipe Wrench Set, Plumber's Grease) and painting items (Oil-Based Wood Stain, Paint Bucket Grid, Brush Set) to increase attachment rate.

Bottom line: the best promotion strategy is a seasonal bundle calendar layered with Redmond-specific precision-tool merchandising. Focus on the highest-frequency pairs first, because the top bundles are recurring, measurable, and already proven by order-share signals between 0.1155% and 0.3113%.
